author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 겨울철새 수천 마리 · 텃새 수십 마리
habitat: 농촌 인가, 산지, 해변 침엽수 등의 높은 나무
summary: 전국에서 흔히 볼 수 있는 텃새로, 농촌 마을이나 산지, 바닷가 침엽수처럼 높은 나무가 있는 곳에 산다. 번식기에는 한두 쌍씩 작게 지내다가 번식이 끝난 겨울철에는 무리를 짓고, 낮에는 홀로 또는 짝지어 다녀도 밤에는 여럿이 모여 자는 일이 많다. 3~6월에 알 3~5개를 낳는다. 다른 새의 알과 새끼, 작은 포유류, 양서·파충류, 갑각류, 곤충과 도토리, 곡식, 열매까지 가리지 않고 먹으며, 국외에서는 중국 남부, 일본 남부, 타이완에 분포한다.

sexes.text: 암수 같은 색이며 암컷이 조금 작다.

art.subject: Carrion Crow (Corvus corone), adult (sexes alike) in early spring: entirely black — head, body, wings and tail — with a subdued metallic gloss that shows greenish to violet-blue in good light on the wings, back and tail; head feathers smooth and tight; black nasal bristles cover the base of the upper mandible; bill black, fairly slender for a crow; dark brown eye; black legs and feet.
art.pose: perched on top of a tall tree, side view
art.scene: tall trees beside Korean farmland and hills in early spring; no people, buildings or text
views: adult in winter or early spring, side view perched on a treetop branch: entirely black with a faint greenish gloss on the wings and back, flat crown running smoothly into a fairly slender straight black bill, black legs, square tail
adult in worn summer plumage, side view perched: still all black but duller, with a slight brownish tinge on the wings and tail, the same flat crown and slender bill
art.build: Large crow, 50cm: bigger and much heavier than a Eurasian Magpie, slightly smaller and slimmer-billed than the Large-billed Crow. Crown rather flat, sloping smoothly into the bill without a steep forehead. Bill black, about as long as the head, fairly straight, the upper mandible curving down gently only near the tip. Legs black and sturdy, medium length; walks with a confident stride. At rest the wingtips reach close to the tail tip. Tail medium-length and square-ended. In flight the wings are broad with fingered tips.
avoid: Do not paint a steep, domed forehead and a very thick, deeply arched bill — that is Large-billed Crow (Corvus macrorhynchos).
Do not paint a bare whitish-grey face around the bill base — that is an adult Rook (Corvus frugilegus).
Do not add a grey collar or grey body (Daurian Jackdaw, Hooded Crow) or a pale eye.
Do not make the tail long or wedge-shaped; it is square-ended and of medium length.
